title: Stable representative mosaic packs for production quant validation
creator: Jordan Patel
description: Create a repeatable, production-safe curation and sampling strategy for calibration packs used in FP8/INT8 quantization and accuracy validation. Goal is to produce compact per-domain 'mosaic' packs that: 1) reflect production distribution across tenants and verticals, 2) preserve rare but high-impact intents, 3) avoid overfitting to a few heavy tenants, and 4) are small enough to run frequent quant regression jobs across model variants and runtimes.
sampling_spec: Hybrid stratified reservoir: allocate initial budget per domain proportional to traffic but enforce minimum per-domain floor
Semantic clustering: embed prompts with on-device encoder and cluster using approx K-Means (K tuned per domain) to capture diversity
Rarity-preserving selection: compute intent rarity score and reserve a fixed quota for top-N rare intents per domain
Recency smoothing: exponential decay on timestamp with half-life parameter (lambda=0.6) to balance freshness and representativeness
Per-tenant caps: enforce max-percentage to prevent a single tenant from dominating a domain pack
Quality filter: remove prompts < 10 tokens or with high error rates (failed parses, toxic content flags) using lightweight heuristics
Pack sizing: target 3k-15k prompts per domain depending on domain entropy and model size budget
validation_plan: Baseline: run current INT8/FP8 profiles on control packs used in previous releases to establish reference metrics
Cross-profile sweep: evaluate mosaic packs across small/medium/large model variants and compare per-domain deltas
Metrics: token-level KL, prompt-level BLEU/ROUGE when applicable, percent exact-match for structured tasks, and custom business metrics (intent accuracy, hallucination-rate)
Rollback thresholds: block deployment if any high-priority domain shows >2.0% absolute degradation or >10% relative degradation in primary metric
A/B holdout: reserve a 5% user-holdout to validate live impact before full rollout
Statistical significance: use bootstrap resampling on per-prompt deltas to estimate 95% CIs for domain aggregates

notes: Trade-off: Increasing rarity quota improves long-tail accuracy but increases pack complexity and build time; mitigated by adaptive K per domain.
Decision: avoid anchor-based exemplar selection to reduce bias introduced by manual curation — use cluster centroids + rare-intent sampling instead.
Operational note: pack builds are offline and scheduled nightly; ensure disk retention of previous 3 builds for revertability.
Risk: rapidly shifting domains (e.g., trending events) may be underrepresented — plan periodic freshness-only mini-packs to capture spikes.
